title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed into a high-traffic event environment they were not designed to handle. The system failed under the combined strain of heavy gridlock, high ambient activity from fireworks displays, and sustained periods of stationary operation that depleted battery reserves faster than the vehicles could manage.

This is a deployment failure, not a model failure. The autonomous vehicles operated as designed but outside the conditions of their training and testing. A human traffic management system, or human override protocols triggered by exceptional congestion alerts, could have prevented vehicles from entering or remaining in areas where battery depletion was foreseeable.

It is not established whether the vehicles' navigation systems were aware of the Fourth of July event density or whether real-time traffic data was available to reroute them before gridlock occurred.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
During Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco on Saturday, several Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded in heavy traffic after their batteries drained while stuck in gridlock following fireworks displays near the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, including Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets with some requiring towing. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion in the area.

The situation caused frustration among other motorists, with some spending nearly two hours in standstill traffic. One passenger reported her Waymo continued driving when fireworks were lit nearby, while another vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks. The company said no injuries occurred and that its roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to meet with stakeholders to improve traffic management for future events, acknowledging that over 100,000 people in the area experienced delays getting home.
